explanation: This head fires on the comma that closes a mid-sentence, comma-opened insertion - an appositive, a non-restrictive relative clause, a participial or prepositional aside, or a reporting tag - and at that closing comma it attends almost one-hot (weight 0.9-1.0) back to the insertion's opening comma. In running text of two or more sentences such closers measure 0.5-1.0 x max (2.5-4.8, the scan's peaks); in a text that is a single short sentence they are weaker (0.2-0.6 x max, 1.0-3.0) and a text opening with an indefinite or demonstrative subject ('A study, ...', 'This report, ...') or a bare name ('John, ...') can land at or just under the 0.25 x max line. Predict inactive: the opening comma of the insertion (0.0-0.1 x max), a sentence whose only comma is a fronted adverbial or prepositional phrase ('However, ', 'In 2019, ', 'After lunch, ', 'According to the map, ') (0.1-0.25 x max; 16 of 16 measured below the line), short comma-free declarative sentences (0.0-0.2 x max; about one in twenty crosses weakly), and sentence-final periods. Do not rely on these as inactive: dash-delimited asides, often active at the closing dash (0.25-0.5 x max); semicolon- or parenthesis-closed and unpaired single commas (0.1-0.25 x max, can cross); and the word directly after a list comma (up to 0.35 x max).
